name: Khalaj

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Khalaj Turkic (turk1303).

notes: Research. Khalaj is a divergent Turkic language of central Iran, here written in a Latin orthography of the Azerbaijani/Turkish type. Consonant and vowel letters are given their conventional Turkic-Latin values, including c (dʒ), ç (tʃ), ş (ʃ), j (ʒ), x (x), ğ (ɣ), q (uvular/back stop), the front-rounded ö and ü, back unrounded ı, and ə. Khalaj is notable for preserving Proto-Turkic word-initial *h and for a phonemic long/short vowel contrast; vowel length is not marked in this map and is left unencoded, and the exact digraph conventions of the source orthography may vary, so a moderate PER floor is expected. Grapheme table checked against Doerfer (1988) / Doerfer (Encyclopaedia Iranica): no discrepancy found.

stress.notes: Like the great majority of Turkic languages, Khalaj places default word stress on the final syllable (Doerfer 1988, Grammatik des Chaladsch); this is the standard pan-Turkic pattern this project already uses for its other Turkic specs. Exceptions conditioned by specific suffixes are not separately encoded here for lack of a Khalaj-specific suffix inventory in the sources consulted.
